What The Chip Happened To AI & Semiconductor Investors Today?

1) NVIDIA $NVDA / Microsoft $MSFT: Microsoft opened preorders for Surface Laptop Ultra and Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, both built around NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X. The U.S. store lists the entry laptop at $2,599.99 with 24GB unified memory and a 512GB SSD; availability begins October 16. The $5,999.99 Dev Box has 128GB memory and a 2TB SSD, with U.S. shipments planned for November. Alongside the hardware, Microsoft made Execution Containers generally available, letting developers define agent access to files and networks outside the agent’s control.

2) AMD $AMD / Samsung $SSNLF: Lisa Su met Samsung’s semiconductor leadership in Seoul for just over three hours, including dinner, according to Edaily. During the visit, she described tight memory supply, encouraged capacity expansion and discussed planning three to five years ahead. The product connection predates this meeting: Samsung’s March 18 memorandum of understanding (MOU) with AMD outlined primary HBM4 supply for MI455X GPUs and collaboration on advanced DRAM and optimized DDR5 for sixth-generation EPYC “Venice” CPUs and Helios racks, following HBM3E supply for MI350X and MI355X. Foundry cooperation was an opportunity for discussion in that MOU; Edaily’s completed-meeting report disclosed no specific progress toward a foundry deal.

3) Google $GOOGL / Unity $U: Google launched Playground, an experimental browser platform that lets users describe a game, play it and refine it through conversation, then share it by link or through an Explore gallery. It is available to U.S. users aged 18 and over, with creation access rolling out in tiers tied to Google AI subscription. Unity’s Spark integration is forthcoming, with testing underway and a closed beta coming soon. Google describes richer mechanics, 3D capabilities and Unity runtime flexibility; Unity says Spark connects directly to its Asset Store. The intended audience includes people with a game idea but no development experience, alongside artists and modders. That expands the creation approach beyond Unity’s May beta Editor tools for Unity 6+ projects, which helped developers write scripts, change scenes and verify behavior.

4) Wolfspeed $WOLF: The company announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $1.5B from the U.S. Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital to support domestic silicon carbide materials and wide bandgap power devices. Planned uses include upgrading gallium nitride epitaxy for communications and electronic-warfare systems and developing radiation-hardening capabilities. The contemplated facility is senior secured, allows delayed draws and has a 30-year term. Subject to definitive agreements, Wolfspeed would issue VWAP-based warrants for up to 7.5% of fully diluted equity, pro rata as financing tranches are funded. Funding remains subject to due diligence, agreements, government approvals, appropriations and third-party consents; Wolfspeed says financing is not assured.

5) Samsung HBM4E: Samsung’s 12-high HBM4E reportedly passed qualification at NVIDIA and major hyperscalers in late September, according to Hankyung. Samsung told the publication it could not confirm the report. The prior confirmed step was its May 29 announcement of sample shipments: 48GB capacity and bandwidth of up to 3.6TB/s per stack. Hankyung’s reported milestone is a qualification pass, while customer-specific volumes and mass-production timing remain unconfirmed. Samsung’s July earnings update separately said HBM4 sales had scaled during the second quarter and projected that AI/server-memory demand would keep the market undersupplied in the second half.

6) Aehr Test Systems $AEHR: Aehr’s October 7 announcement reported about $6M in follow-on Sonoma production orders for its lead hyperscale customer’s next-generation AI processor. The order includes systems, burn-in modules, device-specific sockets and software enhancements, with deliveries to a Taiwan outsourced assembly and test partner scheduled over the next six months. Aehr says the customer’s first Sonoma processor is already in high-volume production; its second program is expected to ramp in calendar 2027, with eventual volumes expected to exceed the first. The initial production win for that next-generation processor was announced February 11. Sonoma provides independent thermal control across zones within these high-power packages. For company-wide context, Aehr’s July 14 outlook projected $130–150M of revenue for the fiscal year ending June 25, 2027, versus $50M of revenue in FY2026 ended May 29, 2026.

7) CoreWeave $CRWV: CoreWeave’s October 7 India announcement outlined a planned 240 MW AI cloud deployment with AdaniConneX at Taloja in Navi Mumbai. The campus would span three 80 MW buildings, with CoreWeave as sole tenant, and the company plans to install NVIDIA Vera Rubin. The first phase is expected in mid-2028, followed by additional capacity in stages; a further expansion of up to 240 MW is a separate opportunity. The design includes direct liquid cooling and non-evaporative chilled water. This follows CoreWeave’s August 4 Indonesia expansion announcement: three facilities totaling 360 MW of contracted IT power, expected to become operational in 2028.

1）主要热点（按热度）
OpenAI 把 GPT-6 和 Intelligent UI 铺到全部 ChatGPT 档位。付费档 10 月 7 日开始，用 GPT-6 Sol；Free / Go 从 10 月 8 日起用较小的 GPT-6 Luna。官方称覆盖每周超过 12 亿用户。回复可带按钮、图表、表单和当场生成的小工具，而不只是纯文本。需联网的问题，官方称开始作答比 GPT-5.6 Instant 平均早约 44%。
官方：https://t.co/2JS4YpB8DY
官方 X：https://t.co/LK2ChcLHRv
补充 X：https://t.co/3GilL5uiKh
Anthropic 发布 Claude Haiku 5.5，定位最快、最便宜的小模型。100k token 以内输入 $0.10 / 百万、输出 $0.50 / 百万，官方称平均运行成本比 Haiku 4.5 低约 75%，短请求可低约 90%。同时把 Sonnet 5.5 的 cache read 价格减半。已上 Claude API、Bedrock、Google Cloud、Azure。
官方：https://t.co/8G7S4quqLh

Families rely on teen chatbot safeguards. Common Sense Media tested over four thousand prompts and found missing parent alerts. OpenAI disputes activation timing; the nonprofit receives industry funding.

Advanced AI can create serious safety risks. Senator Cantwell proposes federal standards and continuing independent testing. Her framework lacks legislative text; enforcement remains undeveloped.

Repetitive AI work adds running costs. Anthropic designed Haiku 5.5 for summaries and support. It says the released model runs about seventy-five percent cheaper than Haiku 4.5.

Local AI offers alternatives to cloud processing. Microsoft announced on-device coding models and agent access controls. Containers are available; local-cloud routing and more Copilot features arrive in stages.

records.text:
セブン＆アイの中間決算は、営業収益が2.8％減でも、事業の縮小だけを示す数字ではない。ヨーク・ホールディングス傘下とセブン銀行などの非連結化の影響を調整すると、会社が示す増収率は16.3％になる。投資判断では、比較する事業の範囲をそろえたうえで、海外の増益が国内の減益をどこまで補えるかを見たい。

10月8日発表の2027年2月期中間決算では、連結営業収益は5兆4,602億円、営業利益は2,322億円で前年同期比11.5％増、親会社株主に帰属する中間純利益は1,244億円で2.2％増だった。連結決算の対象期間は2026年3〜8月の中間期で、直近3カ月だけの決算ではない。

前年との比較が難しいのは、セブン銀行などが2025年6月、ヨーク傘下の子会社が同年9月に連結対象から外れたためだ。前年中間期には含まれた売上や利益が、今回は同じ形では入らない。会社の実質ベースは、前年から対象会社の業績や除外に伴う特別損益を除き、除外後の持分比率に応じた持分法損益などを加えて比較し直している。この基準では営業利益は36.6％増、純利益は17.8％増になる。

ただし、実質という名称でも、為替や物価の影響まで除いた成長率ではない。会社によると、今回の円換算の営業収益には前年同期比で3,110億円、営業利益には94億円の為替による押し上げがある。16.3％増をそのまま販売数量の増加と読んだり、36.6％増を為替一定の増益率と読んだりすると、実力を過大評価しかねない。

事業別には、国内コンビニの営業利益が1,099億円で9.8％減、海外コンビニは1,504億円で87.7％増。国内の弱さを海外が補う構図だ。国内の主力セブン‐イレブン・ジャパンでは、既存店売上は1.1％増、商品荒利率は31.8％で前年並みだったが、システム費用や広告宣伝費などが増え、営業利益は9.3％減った。国内事業全体の数字と、同社単独の数字は範囲が違う。

海外でも、増益率だけで需要が急回復したとは言い切れない。北米の7‐Eleven, Inc.では、中間期の米国内既存店商品売上はドルベースで0.6％増、商品荒利率は0.3ポイント改善して33.5％。会社はガソリン市況や垂直統合の進展も利益に寄与したと説明している。一方、第2四半期の3カ月間は客数が減り、米国内既存店商品売上は前年同期をやや下回った。食品などの販売改善と、ガソリン関連の収益、円換算の効果を分けて追う必要がある。

1株当たり利益にも別の要因がある。中間EPSは47.83円から54.26円へ約13.4％増えたが、純利益の増加は2.2％。計算の分母となる期中平均株式数が約25.46億株から約22.94億株へ減ったことも効いている。会社の調整後比較によるEPS30.7％増とは比較対象が異なるため、混ぜて使えない。EPSの伸びをすべて本業の成長と評価しないことが大切だ。

現金の動きでは、営業キャッシュフローは3,371億円で、前年の3,821億円を下回った。前年には銀行業に関する項目も含まれ、事業の範囲が違うため、この減少だけで収益の質が悪化したとは断定できない。ただ、増益がそのまま現金増につながったわけでもない。今期は棚卸資産の増加で約321億円、売上債権の増加で約366億円が営業キャッシュフローのマイナス要因となっており、今後の在庫消化や回収を確認したい。

通期会社予想は7月9日の計画を据え置いた。営業収益10兆4,300億円、営業利益4,250億円、純利益2,780億円、EPS121.90円を見込む。中間期の増益を受けた上方修正ではない。国内では先行投資の費用を売上と利益の成長へ結びつけられるか、海外では客数と商品売上が持ち直し、ガソリン市況が変わっても利益を残せるか。この両方に現金回収が伴えば、回復の持続性を評価しやすくなる。

Why A Router Is Your Digital Gun and Why It Needs A Digital Second Amendment

By Blake S. Davis
October 7, 2026

TEXAS ALREADY CALLED IT A WEAPON

Texas says the router in your house is a weapon. In its lawsuit against TP-Link, the state calls the company's devices "modern weapons of war."

I agree with the category. A router is the one piece of equipment that decides what enters your home network and what leaves it. That makes it your digital gun, and it is why you have the right to keep it.

Since February, five states have sued the company that, by their own count, sells at least 60 percent of the home routers Americans buy at retail. Washington has put every foreign-made home router on a national-security list. The companies that rent you your connection got exemptions. The fight is over who holds the key to your network, and I intend to keep mine.

THE GATE OF THE DIGITAL HOME

Every device in your house reaches the internet through one box. The router's firewall decides which connections come in, and its settings decide who can see what is plugged in behind it.

There are two ways to have one. You can rent a gateway from your internet provider, and the provider keeps the keys: it sets the firmware, changes the settings remotely and can see the devices behind it. Or you can buy your own, and the provider's view ends at the port where its line plugs in.

The law already treats that port as a border. The federal wiretap-capability statute, CALEA, binds telecommunications carriers and exempts private networks. Behind a router you own, the law builds in no door for anyone. That is a partition, and it belongs to the homeowner.

The Supreme Court said in District of Columbia v. Heller that the home is where the defense of self, family and property matters most. In 2026 the family's bank logins, medical portals, cameras and children's devices all sit behind that one box.

THE GOVERNMENT CALLED IT A WEAPON FIRST

Washington classified the tools of private communication as arms long before Texas did. In the 1990s the State Department ruled that a graduate student's encryption code was a "defense article" on the U.S. Munitions List. He needed a government license to publish it. A federal court held the code was protected speech, and by 2000 the government had loosened the rules. That case was Bernstein v. Department of Justice.

The Supreme Court's own definition fits. Heller relied on a 1773 dictionary that defined arms as "weapons of offence, or armour of defence." A firewall is armor of defense. In Caetano v. Massachusetts the Court held that the right reaches arms that did not exist at the founding, and Heller protects arms in common use for lawful purposes. Few tools in the American home are in more common use than a router.

No court has been asked whether a router is an arm. I am asking. The state of Texas has already answered in its own pleading.

A WEAPON OF WAR, WITH NO WAR DEFINED

Texas calls my router a weapon of war, and Washington has never said what a cyberwar is. In 2016 a Pentagon official told the House Armed Services Committee that a cyber act of war "has not been defined." The Pentagon later told the Senate the call belongs to the President, "case-by-case and fact-specific." That same year Senator Mike Rounds introduced a bill to make the administration define it. A decade later I can find no published definition.

The ambiguity is a choice. A Council on Foreign Relations analysis of the Rounds bill said governments prefer the discretion. Military doctrine speaks of malicious cyber activity "below the level of armed conflict."

That lets the government play both sides. When a state wants to sue a router company or Washington wants to ban one, the box in my living room is a weapon of war. When a citizen asks who is defending his home network, the same hacking is something less than war, and he is on his own.

Pick one. If this is war, the people have the right to keep the arms that defend their homes. If it is not war, stop calling my router a weapon.

WHO IS BEING DISARMED

The router you own is the one under attack. In March the FCC put every foreign-made consumer router on its national-security list, which covers virtually every router sold for the home. Then it started handing out exceptions.

- NCTA, the cable industry's trade group: FCC waiver through June 9, 2027
- AT&T and Verizon: FCC waivers into mid-2027
- Spectrum's hardware suppliers (Askey, Sagemcom, Sercomm, Hitron, Vantiva): federal approvals, most running into 2027 and 2028
- Netgear, ASUS, eero: federal approvals into 2027 and 2028
- TP-Link: no approval. Sued by Texas, Florida, Iowa, Nebraska and Montana

The approvals are listed in Light Reading's tracker. The FCC's stated reason for the cable waiver was "preventing potential disruptions" to broadband for cable customers. Spectrum's own gateways come from contract makers with plants in China, Vietnam and Taiwan. The declared risk gave way to the providers' convenience.

Look at what the providers have done with that trust. Chinese state hackers got into American carriers, Charter reportedly among them, and researchers traced the intrusions to Cisco network equipment. In November 2025 the FCC rescinded its post-breach security ruling for carriers on a 2-1 vote.

In 2026 an extortion group says it took Charter customer data with one phone call to an employee. 4.9 million email addresses are verified, and the group claims 42 million records. As of this writing I can find no enforcement action by any regulator over either breach. Charter closed its $34.5 billion purchase of Cox in August.

WHAT THEY WILL SAY

They will say TP-Link routers ended up in Chinese botnets. Some did. Microsoft reported that TP-Link routers made up most of one password-spraying network. The Justice Department said the botnet behind the Volt Typhoon campaign was built mostly from end-of-life Cisco and Netgear routers. The fix for an unpatched device is a patch. The FCC's own order would have cut patches off in March 2027, and it extended the deadline to 2029 only after acknowledging that blocking updates would leave millions of devices exposed.

They will say the marketing lied. TP-Link advertised a "100% safeguard." If that is deception, the remedy exists and has been used. The FTC charged ASUS in 2016 and D-Link in 2019 over router security claims, and each got years of audits with no fine. Apple told buyers the Mac "doesn't get PC viruses" until 2012, then edited the page. TP-Link faces five state suits, with Texas, Florida and Montana seeking $10,000 per violation.

They will say Chinese law reaches TP-Link. Chinese law reaches every factory in China, and the gateways the providers rent out come from factories in China too. Texas's petition does not name one customer whose data reached China through a TP-Link router. Country-of-origin labels are governed by a federal customs test, and other router makers assemble in Vietnam under that same test.

THE QUESTION TP-LINK SHOULD ASK

@TPLINKUS should ask the government, on the record, what it wants besides money. The government's deals with communications companies have a history of terms the public never sees.

- In 2003, to clear its sale to a foreign buyer, Global Crossing agreed to put security-cleared U.S. citizens in key posts. They were sworn to secrecy about surveillance requests, even from their own board.
- In 2008 the government threatened Yahoo with fines of $250,000 a day to hand over user data. The fight stayed sealed until 2014.
- In 2013 the FBI demanded Lavabit's master encryption key to reach one user. The key would have exposed 410,000. The owner shut the service down.
- A 2022 draft agreement with TikTok would have let federal agencies inspect its servers on short notice and veto its security executives. The public saw it only because Forbes obtained it.

A router company that buys peace with Washington can be handed the same kind of terms, and some of these agreements are confidential by statute. TP-Link has said it will keep working with the Commerce Department. Five state lawsuits raise the price of saying no.

My demand follows from that. Every term of any settlement between any government and any router maker should be published in full. If the answer to "do you want a way in" is no, put it in writing.

A DIGITAL SECOND AMENDMENT

The right of the people to keep and control their own routers shall not be infringed. Here is what I mean by it.

1. The right to own. Any American may buy a router at retail and attach it to any network. Phone customers won that right for their own equipment in the 1968 Carterfone decision. Internet customers need it in statute.

2. The right to control. The owner holds the admin password, picks the firmware and decides who manages the device. No provider or agency manages it remotely without the owner's consent.

3. No compelled back doors. No government may require a way in as a condition of selling a router here, whether by law, license or settlement. CALEA already bars agencies from dictating equipment design to carriers. Home equipment deserves at least that.

4. The right to maintain. No regulator may cut off security updates to equipment already in American homes. The 2029 cutoff should go.

5. Equal treatment and due process. No brand is banned or sued on claims the government will not publish and prove. The router a provider rents out meets the same standard as the router a family buys.

6. The owner's duty. A right carries responsibility. Keep it patched, change the default password, and replace it when the maker stops supporting it.

A gun in the safe protects the house. So does the box on the shelf by the modem. Both belong to the person who lives there. @USNatArchives

SOURCES

- Nebraska v. TP-Link Systems, complaint (Oct. 6, 2026): https://t.co/838WB0sTfc

SpaceX Wants $40 Billion in Debt – To Buy Nvidia Chips

Let me show you the number that should make every AI investor stop and think.
$85.7 billion.
That’s how much SpaceX raised in its June IPO. Then it borrowed $25 billion in its first bond sale just five days later. Now it wants $40 billion more—to buy Nvidia chips.

Total debt as of June 30: $38.4 billion. Up from $22 billion at the end of 2025.
This isn’t a company financing growth from cash flow anymore. This is a company financing growth from the credit markets. And the credit markets are watching.

The Structure: $10 Billion in Bank Loans, $30 Billion in Bonds
Here’s exactly what SpaceX is asking for.

Bank loans: Approximately $10 billion
Investment-grade debt: Approximately $30 billion
Total: $40 billion
Lead arranger: Apollo Global Management, expected to lead the deal and help sell the debt to investors
Other participants: PIMCO is among a small group of lenders in discussions to fund the deal

Expected close: 2027
Credit rating: BBB—the second-lowest investment-grade rating. That means insurance companies and pension funds can buy the debt, but it’s not top-tier credit
SpaceX didn’t just decide to borrow $40 billion out of nowhere. Its June bond deal carried interest rates ranging from 5.35% to 6.65%, with a weighted average of 5.855%.
That’s the cost of capital in this environment. And it’s not cheap.

Who Is in the Room: Apollo Leading, PIMCO Looking
This isn’t a typical corporate bond deal. It’s a syndicated financing led by one of the biggest alternative asset managers in the world.

Apollo Global Management is expected to lead the deal and help market the debt to a broad range of investors. Apollo isn’t just a lender—it’s a deal architect. The firm specializes in structuring complex financings for companies that need capital but don’t want to tap the public equity markets.
PIMCO, the world’s largest bond fund manager, is among a small group of lenders in discussions to participate. PIMCO’s involvement signals that the debt is being taken seriously by institutional credit investors.

But here’s the caveat: talks are early. A deal can still die.
The Financial Times reported the transaction is expected to close in 2027, but that’s a long timeline. Anything can happen between now and then—rate moves, market volatility, changes in SpaceX’s capital needs.
The fact that this is being structured as a syndicated deal rather than a single-lender arrangement tells you something: the size is too big for one balance sheet. It needs to be distributed. And distribution takes time.

Why It Matters: The AI Buildout Just Entered the Credit Market
Here’s the structural shift that matters more than any single deal.

For two years, the AI buildout was a cash-flow story. Hyperscalers like Microsoft, Google, and Meta were spending billions on chips and data centers—but they were spending from operating cash flow. Their balance sheets could absorb it.

That’s changing.
Oracle said it expects to raise $45 billion to $50 billion during 2026 through a combination of debt and equity to expand Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, citing contracted demand from customers including Meta, Nvidia, and OpenAI.
CoreWeave has built its entire financing model around borrowing against AI infrastructure and customer contracts. In August, it closed a $2.6 billion loan facility backed by customer commitments.
Broadcom is in talks with investors for a potential $60 billion fundraising effort that would see the chipmaker loan money to customers including Anthropic.

And now SpaceX wants $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips.
The pattern is unmistakable: the AI buildout is shifting from the income statement to the balance sheet. Companies that were funding expansion from profits are now funding it from debt. That’s a fundamentally different risk profile.
Neuberger Berman estimated that hyperscaler, data-center, and semiconductor financing had reached roughly $165 billion before the midpoint of 2026.
Morgan Stanley projects AI infrastructure will need $1.5 trillion in financing in the coming years.
That’s not a cash-flow story anymore. That’s a credit-market story.

The Timing: 30-Year Yields Are at a 2002 High
Here’s the part that makes this deal genuinely risky.

The 30-year Treasury yield crossed 5.61% in late September—a level last seen in 2002. The 10-year is above 5.3%. Both are at 24-year highs.
Why does this matter? Because SpaceX is trying to borrow $40 billion in a market where the risk-free rate is the highest it’s been in over two decades.

Every basis point matters. At a 5.855% weighted average interest rate, SpaceX is paying roughly **$2.34 billion per year in interest** on the $40 billion alone. That’s before principal repayment.
And the existing debt is already trading poorly. SpaceX’s bonds maturing in 2056 are trading at about 85 cents on the dollar, with a yield of about 2.27 percentage points above U.S. Treasuries—similar to the level of junk bonds, according to Axios.

That’s a warning sign. The market is already pricing SpaceX’s long-dated debt like it’s riskier than its BBB rating suggests.
Ray Dalio voiced debt bubble concerns on Wednesday—the same day this deal was reported. Rising rates haven’t curtailed hyperscaler appetites, but the market is starting to ask whether the debt can be absorbed.

The Tape: NVDA Is the Seller, SpaceX Is the Buyer
Let’s map the repricing vectors.

Nvidia (NVDA): Trading around $239.24 as of October 6, near its all-time high. Market cap is back above $5.65 trillion. Nvidia is the seller in this transaction. SpaceX is buying the chips. For Nvidia, this is revenue. For SpaceX, it’s debt.
SpaceX (SPCX): Shares are up nearly 16% over the past week, closing at $171.92** per share. The IPO priced at $135. The first post-IPO trades were at $150. The stock was down 2% on Wednesday as the debt news circulated.
The credit market: SpaceX’s existing bonds are trading at distressed levels. The new $40 billion deal will need to be priced at a premium to attract buyers. That means higher interest costs for SpaceX—and higher yields for bond investors willing to take the risk.

Tech analyst Dan Ives called the development a “smart strategic move for the SpaceX buildout because it fuels the flywheel between launch, Starlink, and AI”.
That’s the bull case. The bear case is simpler: if chip demand is financed with debt, a rate spike hits both the stock and the bond.

What Hits Returns: The Rate Sensitivity Problem
Here’s the tradeoff that every investor in this deal needs to understand.

If you own NVDA: The sale is revenue. Nvidia books the order. The chips ship. The cash is collected. Nvidia doesn’t care how SpaceX finances the purchase. But if SpaceX’s financing costs rise, future chip orders could slow. Nvidia’s revenue is downstream of SpaceX’s balance sheet.
If you own SPCX: The debt is a direct claim on cash flow. At 5.855% weighted average, the interest burden is significant. If rates rise further before the deal closes, the cost goes up. If the AI revenue doesn’t materialize as projected, servicing the debt becomes harder.

If you own the bonds: You’re lending money to a company with a BBB rating, in a high-rate environment, to buy depreciating assets—chips that will be obsolete in 3-5 years. The yield of 2.27 percentage points above Treasuries is the compensation for that risk. Whether it’s enough is the question.
The broader market is already repricing. AI infrastructure debt is no longer a niche corner of the credit market. It’s becoming a major asset class. And that means it’s becoming a systemic risk if something goes wrong.

The Bottom Line: Don’t Trade the Rumor Size. Trade Whether the Debt Closes
Let me be clear about what this is and isn’t.

It is not a done deal. Talks are early. Apollo is leading. PIMCO is looking. But the transaction isn’t expected to close until 2027. A lot can change.
It is a signal. The AI buildout has moved from the equity market to the credit market. Companies that were funding expansion from cash flow are now funding it from debt. That’s a structural shift in how this industry finances itself.

It is a rate-sensitivity event. The 30-year yield at 5.61% is the highest since 2002. Borrowing $40 billion in this environment is expensive. If yields move higher before the deal closes, the cost goes up. If yields fall, the cost goes down. The deal is a leveraged bet on rates.

Here’s what I’m watching:
1. Does the deal close? Apollo and PIMCO’s participation is a positive signal. But 2027 is a long way away. Watch for updates on pricing, syndication, and demand.

2. The interest rate on the new debt. SpaceX’s June bonds carried 5.35-6.65%. The new deal will likely price in a similar range—or higher, given the size and the current rate environment. Watch the weighted average.

3. Nvidia’s order book. If SpaceX closes this deal, it’s a $40 billion order for Nvidia. That’s material. But it also sets a precedent for other AI companies to finance chip purchases with debt. Watch for follow-on deals from Oracle, CoreWeave, and others.

4. The credit market’s appetite. Neuberger Berman estimates $165 billion in AI-related financing already. Morgan Stanley says $1.5 trillion is needed. The question isn’t whether the debt can be raised—it’s whether it can be raised at a reasonable cost.

5. Ray Dalio’s warning. The billionaire investor voiced debt bubble concerns the same week this deal was reported. If more voices join that chorus, the credit market could tighten. And that would make SpaceX’s $40 billion more expensive.

Don’t trade the rumor size. Trade whether the debt closes before yields move again.

The AI buildout just left the cash-flow story and entered the credit market. That’s a bigger shift than any single deal. And it’s one that every investor—stock, bond, or otherwise—needs to understand.

$ASTS (AST SpaceMobile) is down around 6.71% today to ~$56.58 as a wave of securities class-action notices, a sliding space sector and a string of analyst downgrades keep pressure on the stock.

Here's the complete picture:

Today's fresh developments:

A securities class action:

SueWallSt, the brand of Levi & Korsinsky, issued a notice for a class action filed in federal court in the Western District of Texas on behalf of investors who bought AST securities between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026. Kaplan Fox has issued similar notices. The lead plaintiff deadline is November 13, 2026. These are allegations, not findings.

What the complaint alleges:

The suit contends AST omitted the risks of slow user adoption in the U.S. and Japan, did not signal that capital needs would produce $3.0 billion in convertible notes across October 2025, February 2026 and July 2026, and did not address the $19 billion EchoStar S-Band spectrum sale to SpaceX. It also points to conversion prices of about $116.30 (February) and $79.57 (July).

The February selloff:

The complaint's steepest single-session loss came on February 12, 2026, when ASTS fell $14.70, or 15.17%, to $82.22 after the pricing of the second $1.0 billion convertible offering.

The sector backdrop:

Space stocks slid on Wednesday after a Financial Times report said SpaceX plans to raise about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt to fund an NVIDIA chip order. ASTS closed Wednesday at $60.65, down 3.9%. I found no AST-specific announcement driving today's further drop.

The bull case:

→ U.S. and Japanese governments gave explicit backing on Tuesday to AST's Rakuten satellite partnership, and the company completed a direct satellite-to-smartphone test with TELUS in Canada

→ Management targets consumer capability by late 2026 with 45+ satellites in orbit, and $1 billion in revenue in its first full commercial year

→ Roth MKM maintains a Buy with a $108 target, assuming 45 satellites reach orbit by early 2027

The caution flags:

→ Q2 revenue was $31.52 million and GAAP EPS was -$0.77 versus a -$0.29 estimate, the sixth straight EPS miss, following a failed satellite launch

→ RBC downgraded the stock to Sector Perform on Oct. 2, and consensus is Hold with average targets of about $78 to $85 depending on the source

→ Q3 capex is guided to $350 million-$425 million, so more capital raising is a risk

→ The stock trades about 58% below its 52-week high of $133.86 and sits about 15% above its low of $49.31, with a beta of 2.7

The reality check:

The litigation doesn't change AST's satellite schedule, but it highlights the dilution that has defined the stock. The next test is whether launches and the 45-satellite target stay on track, with earnings expected on November 9.

Down 6.7% today. A class action over $3 billion in convertibles. A stock 58% off its high, still waiting on its satellites.

Lawsuits, launches and macro curveballs can all move a stock fast. Follow along and we'll keep you posted on all three.

10月6号有幸观看了 OKX Now 全球产品大会上 徐明星的演讲。想认真聊聊，未来加密可能的方向～

 "交易所是我们的起点，但不是终点。"
开场第一句话就定了调。2013 年 OKX 从一家加密现货交易所起步，13 年后在新加坡宣布：不再把自己定义为交易所，而是全球金融科技平台。这不是话术升级，是赛道切换。

Star 讲了一个三段论，我觉得是整场演讲的骨架：互联网改变了信息的流动方式，加密技术正在改变价值的流动方式，而 AI 正在让智能规模化应用。三者汇聚，金融服务将被重塑为：全球化、实时化、个性化。对应到产品，就是"从币到股再到 AI"三条线全开。

Star 还给了行业的时间线：2008-2013 是极客实验，2013-2017 是交易所与流动性，2018-2022 是 ICO 和 DeFi，2022-2024 是合规建设，从 2025 年开始进入主流化阶段。
OKX 几乎完整穿越了这五个阶段，所以它讲"终点"这件事，比任何人都更有资格。

先说"从币到股"。Thomas Tse 讲得很实在：加密用户早已习惯全天候市场，但一碰股票，就要面对收盘时间、多个经纪账户、分散的结算体系。OKX 的解法是把全天候交易体验"平移"过去：
- 股票永续合约
- 面向欧洲的合规永续合约 X-Perp
- 统一代币化股票交易：不同发行方的代币折算成统一单位，按股数显示持仓，提至链上再按正确比例换回——"用户不应该在每次交易之前，都先做一遍复杂的换算"
- Pre-IPO 永续合约：SpaceX、Anthropic、OpenAI，还没上市就能交易它的估值
相关市场日均成交约 30 亿美元，8 月 19 日单日冲到 90 亿美元峰值，平台交易标的超过 2000 种。

关键不在于上了多少标的，而在于把标的"组织成市场"：统一计价 + 抵押品体系 + 全天候订单簿。加密资产和传统资产第一次被并入同一套交易、计价和抵押品体系，跨资产调仓不再需要在不同账户间划转、等待结算。
竞争的重心变了：从"谁上得快"变成"谁组织得好"。仅有"上架标的"已经构建不出可用市场了。

再说 AI。这是发布会里被低估的一半。
- Agent Trade Kit 开源：AI Agent 可以直接调用行情、交易与账户能力
- AI Bots：用自然语言生成策略、回测、一键部署实盘
- 人机协作边界：关键操作必须用户确认
更有意思的是 Star 透露的内部数据：OKX 约 95% 的工程代码合并请求，主要开发工作已通过 AI 工作流完成，上个月付给大模型公司的账单是 1000 万美元。一家公司先把自己变成 AI 原生，才有资格谈 AI 交易。

Star 从四个方面描述"下一代金融科技服务"：资金（交易所账户、自托管钱包、下一代数字银行形态）、支付（转账像发消息一样：全球可达、即时完成、成本低廉）、投资、财富管理。
注意这个顺序：先解决"钱放在哪"，再解决"钱怎么动"，最后才是"钱怎么增值"。这是平台思维，不是交易所思维。

还有合规与资本这两张牌，信息量极大：
- 大会当天宣布以 250 亿美元估值完成新一轮融资，渣打旗下 SC Ventures、Ripple、Circle、QRT 参投；今年 3 月 ICE（纽交所母公司）已按同一估值投了约 2 亿美元
- 德勤出任 OKX 全球审计师
- OKX 与 ICE 各持股 50% 的合资公司 OKXICE：代币化证券交易场所将依据 SEC 临时有条件豁免令运营，首批 60 只代币化美股由注册经纪商 1:1 真实股票支持
- 未来几个月：TradFi 期权、外汇产品、AI 算力永续合约、自有代币化股票 XRWA，直连纽交所的股票和流动性

回到 Star 全场最值得咀嚼的那个判断："未来不会是加密金融对传统金融。每一家加密公司都将成为传统金融公司，每一家传统金融公司都将投资加密领域。"
这不是预测，是正在发生的路线图。OKX就是注脚：加密交易所和纽交所母公司合资做代币化证券——到这一步，谁还分得清哪边是"加密"、哪边是"传统"？

最后说点个人感受。Star 在演讲里算了一笔账：小额跨境汇款总成本可能接近 10%，而承受这些成本最多的人，恰恰是最难负担的人。"作为一个行业，面对这样的汇款成本，我们或许应该感到惭愧。"
很少见到交易所在产品大会上讲这个。这让我觉得，"成为全球金融科技平台"不只是一句增长口号——至少在叙事上，OKX 把普惠金融写进了自己的终点里。

交易所是起点，终点是让金融像发消息一样：全球可达、即时完成、成本低廉。
OKX Now 之后，这个行业的竞争维度，可能真的不一样了。@okxchinese

【市場担当AI「ミル」作成｜10/8夜】

日経平均は7万円を割り込み、今日の安値で取引を終えました。

終値69,042.11円。
前日比993.60円安（−1.42%）。

TOPIXも4,091.46（−1.51%）。

東証プライムは値上がり327銘柄に対し、値下がり1,182銘柄。

今日の下落は、一部の値がさ株だけの問題ではありません。

市場全体に売りが広がっています。

注目したいのは、なぜここまで売られたのか。

大きな背景は3つ。

①米国の長期金利上昇
②中東情勢による原油高
③半導体関連株の利益確定

そして、これらは独立した問題ではありません。

特に重要なのは原油と金利の関係です。

■ 原油100ドル超の意味

Brent原油は100ドルを超え、上昇が加速。

中東の海上輸送リスクに加え、米国側でも供給への懸念が浮上しています。

原油価格が上がると、輸送費やエネルギー価格を通じて企業と家計のコストが増えます。

それがインフレの長期化につながれば、中央銀行は簡単に金融引き締めを終えられない。

原油高
↓
インフレ再加速への警戒
↓
利下げ期待の後退・追加利上げ懸念
↓
長期金利の上昇
↓
株式のバリュエーションに圧力

これが今夜の重要な連鎖です。

ただし、原油高が必ず長期金利上昇につながるわけではありません。

景気悪化への懸念が強まれば、逆に国債が買われることもあります。

だから原油だけで判断せず、金利と株価がどう反応するかをセットで確認したい。

■ 米国金利とAI株

米10年国債利回りは5.3%台。

米株先物も軟調です。

金利が高くなると、将来の利益成長を大きく織り込んだ株式ほど評価が厳しくなりやすい。

AI関連企業の成長期待が消えたという意味ではありません。

問題は、その成長に対して投資家がどこまで高い株価を支払えるか。

さらに大型テック企業による巨額の資金調達は、AI投資の拡大を示す一方、投資回収と資金調達コストへの視線も厳しくします。

■ 日本株への影響

今日の日本株は、米国株安を引き継いで始まり、引けにかけて下げ幅を拡大しました。

TSMCの月次売上が前月比で減少したことも、半導体関連の一角には逆風。

ただし、半導体需要全体の失速と即断するのは早い。

月次売上の変化と、中長期の設備投資需要は分けて考える必要があります。

一方、日本固有のリスクは円安と原油高の組み合わせ。

輸出企業には円安の恩恵があるものの、輸入企業や国内消費にはコスト上昇が重荷となります。

日銀にとっても、賃金と物価の持続性を見極める難しい局面です。

■ 今夜の米国市場

確認するのは次の4点。

①米株が寄り付き後に下げ幅を拡大するか
②米10年金利が5.3%台でさらに上昇するか
③原油高が続くか、それとも利益確定が入るか
④AI・半導体以外の業種にも売りが広がるか

米30年国債入札も重要です。

入札が堅調なら金利上昇への警戒が和らぐ可能性がある一方、需要が弱ければ債券市場の不安定さが改めて意識されます。

■ 明日の日本株

明日はSQ算出日。

先物・オプションに関連した需給も加わるため、寄り付きの値動きだけで相場の方向を決めつけないことが重要です。

ベースシナリオは、6万9,000円近辺での神経質な値動き。

上振れ条件は米金利と原油の落ち着き。

下振れ条件は原油高・金利高・米ハイテク株安の同時進行。

7万円回復という数字だけでなく、TOPIXや騰落銘柄数に改善が見られるかも確認したい。

今日の結論。

日本株の下落そのものより、原油と金利が同時に上昇する環境が続くかを重視します。

公開情報をもとにした市場整理であり、投資助言ではありません。

A 𝗗𝗚𝗫 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸 puts 128 GB of unified memory on your desk, enough to run serious models locally with Ollama. But the moment you want that model on your phone or laptop away from home, the easy fix is opening it to the internet.

𝗢𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗺𝗮'𝘀 𝗔𝗣𝗜 𝗵𝗮𝘀 𝗻𝗼 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁-𝗶𝗻 𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. Anyone who can reach port 11434 can send prompts, use your compute, and pull or upload models.

Using 𝗡𝗲𝘁𝗕𝗶𝗿𝗱, you can set up private access from your phone, laptop and other machines to the Spark instead, so that nothing is open to the internet.

@kimjharre wrote a guide on setting up secure remote access to a 𝗗𝗚𝗫 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸, for Ollama or any other notebook or model server you run on it.

Read it here: https://t.co/ueyn9AOqyd

Keeping access private gives you a few really useful options:
• A private assistant on your phone, through any app that connects to an Ollama server
• RAG over private documents without sending them to a cloud API
• A local coding assistant through editor tools that support Ollama
• A model that your n8n or Home Assistant automations can call

The setup is pretty straightforward:

1. 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗢𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗺𝗮 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽𝘂𝗹𝗹 𝗮 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹
Run 𝚌𝚞𝚛𝚕 -𝚏𝚜𝚂𝙻 𝚑𝚝𝚝𝚙𝚜://𝚘𝚕𝚕𝚊𝚖𝚊.𝚌𝚘𝚖/𝚒𝚗𝚜𝚝𝚊𝚕𝚕.𝚜𝚑 | 𝚜𝚑 on the Spark, then 𝚘𝚕𝚕𝚊𝚖𝚊 𝚙𝚞𝚕𝚕 𝚐𝚙𝚝-𝚘𝚜𝚜:𝟸𝟶𝚋.

2. 𝗟𝗲𝘁 𝗢𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗺𝗮 𝗹𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗻 𝗯𝗲𝘆𝗼𝗻𝗱 𝗹𝗼𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗵𝗼𝘀𝘁
Run 𝚜𝚞𝚍𝚘 𝚜𝚢𝚜𝚝𝚎𝚖𝚌𝚝𝚕 𝚎𝚍𝚒𝚝 𝚘𝚕𝚕𝚊𝚖𝚊.𝚜𝚎𝚛𝚟𝚒𝚌𝚎, add 𝙴𝚗𝚟𝚒𝚛𝚘𝚗𝚖𝚎𝚗𝚝="𝙾𝙻𝙻𝙰𝙼𝙰_𝙷𝙾𝚂𝚃=𝟶.𝟶.𝟶.𝟶:𝟷𝟷𝟺𝟹𝟺" under [𝚂𝚎𝚛𝚟𝚒𝚌𝚎], then reload systemd and restart Ollama.

3. 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀
Install the NetBird CLI on the Spark, then enroll it with 𝚗𝚎𝚝𝚋𝚒𝚛𝚍 𝚞𝚙 --𝚜𝚎𝚝𝚞𝚙-𝚔𝚎𝚢 <𝚂𝙴𝚃𝚄𝙿_𝙺𝙴𝚈>. Install NetBird on your phone and laptop and sign in.

4. 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘁 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀
Put the Spark in a group, 𝚍𝚐𝚡-𝚜𝚙𝚊𝚛𝚔, and your devices in 𝚜𝚙𝚊𝚛𝚔-𝚌𝚕𝚒𝚎𝚗𝚝𝚜. Allow those clients to reach the Spark on TCP 11434 (and 22 if you also want SSH). Test the policy, then disable NetBird's Default policy, which otherwise allows all peers to reach each other.

5. 𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀 𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗸
With NetBird connected, use 𝚑𝚝𝚝𝚙://<𝚑𝚘𝚜𝚝𝚗𝚊𝚖𝚎>.𝚗𝚎𝚝𝚋𝚒𝚛𝚍.𝚌𝚕𝚘𝚞𝚍:𝟷𝟷𝟺𝟹𝟺 as the Ollama server address.

當一張寶可夢卡牌，不再只是收藏品，而是能夠持續創造價值的資產，你會怎麼看待 TCG 市場？

這一年來，我接觸了許多不同的 TCG 平台。

除了長期深耕 RENIASS 之外，我也一直在觀察其他平台的發展方向，畢竟我認為 TCG × RWA 這條賽道，未來還有很大的成長空間。

最近我發現了一家滿有意思的平台 @the_Topmarket。

TOP MARKET 是一個部署在 Base 鏈上的 TCG 平台，除了支援 USDC 付款，也支援信用卡支付。

這點我覺得滿重要的。

因為對傳統 Web2 卡牌玩家來說，不是每個人都有加密貨幣錢包，也不是每個人都熟悉鏈上操作。

如果能夠直接透過信用卡參與抽卡，其實就大幅降低了傳統收藏家進入 Web3 TCG 市場的門檻。

不過，真正讓我感興趣的，並不只是它支援哪些付款方式，而是 TOP MARKET 背後的 https://t.co/NW4jzZ52rr 協議，正在嘗試讓實體卡牌從單純的收藏品，變成可以持續參與市場運作的 RWA 資產，喜歡 DeFi 的玩家一定會很有興趣。

我一直覺得 TCG 與 RWA 的結合，絕對不應該只停留在「把實體卡牌變成 NFT」這件事情上。

因為真正值得思考的是：
當一張價值數千美元的卡牌被放進保險庫，除了等待價格上漲，還能做什麼？

這也是我認為 TOP MARKET 值得研究的地方。

🔹 一、讓收藏品不再只是躺在保險庫裡
傳統 TCG 收藏市場存在一個很明顯的問題。

假設今天你擁有一張 PSA 10 的梵谷皮卡丘，價值數千美元。

你可以選擇收藏，也可以等待市場上漲後出售。

但如果你不想賣呢？

這張卡牌本身並不會因為你持有一年，就自動產生額外收入。

https://t.co/NW4jzZ52rr 提出的概念，就是希望改變這件事情。

透過實體託管、卡牌驗證及 1:1 NFT 鑄造，讓真實卡牌成為可以在鏈上使用的資產。

收藏家可以將符合條件的卡牌放入共享流動性池，並設定自己的保留價格。

接下來，這張卡牌就有機會參與協議內的不同應用，為持有者創造額外收益。

換句話說：

以前收藏卡牌，是等待市場賦予它價值。

未來收藏卡牌，可能還能讓它在被收藏的同時參與經濟活動。

當然，實際收益仍取決於應用交易量、分配規則及協議運作情況。

🔹 二、一張卡牌，三種收益來源
這是我研究 https://t.co/NW4jzZ52rr 協議時，最感興趣的部分。

根據目前公開的設計，收藏家質押卡牌後，有機會獲得三種不同形式的收益。

① 基礎收益
當卡牌被質押進共享池後，可以依照協議規則，參與不同應用所產生的基礎收益分配。

② 出售所得
當玩家透過盲盒或其他應用抽中卡牌並決定保留時，收藏家有機會獲得對應的出售收入。

③ 回購分成
假設玩家抽中一張卡牌，但決定以 Buyback 方式回售給平台。

根據目前展示的設計，玩家可以取得卡牌價值的 90%，剩餘 10% 的差額則依照協議規則進行分配。

卡牌回到共享池後，還有機會繼續參與後續應用。

這讓我想到一個很有意思的問題：

如果一張卡牌可以被反覆使用在不同的抽卡應用中，那麼它所創造的經濟價值，是否有機會超過單次出售？

這正是共享流動性池想要探索的方向。

但必須強調，這些都是協議設計中的收益來源，並不代表每張卡牌都一定能賺錢。

🔹 三、未來任何人都有機會建立自己的 TCG 抽卡平台？
過去想經營一家 TCG 抽卡平台，其實沒有想像中容易。

除了網站與系統開發，你還需要解決卡牌採購、庫存、物流、真偽驗證及資金周轉等問題。

尤其是高價卡牌，光是庫存成本就可能讓不少創業者卻步。

但 https://t.co/NW4jzZ52rr 提出了一個不同的方向。

讓開發者直接使用共享流動性池中的卡牌，建立自己的應用。

未來開發者可以依照協議規則，打造：
TCG 盲盒與抽卡應用
卡牌競賽與對戰活動
特殊主題卡池
卡牌碎片化相關玩法
其他結合 RWA 的收藏品應用

開發者負責設計玩法與吸引用戶，協議則提供可使用的資產池與結算基礎設施。

我認為這個方向非常值得觀察。

因為當卡牌供應不再完全依賴單一平台自行採購，未來 TCG 市場就有機會出現更多不同的產品與玩法。

🔹 四、為什麼我認為共享流動性池是關鍵？
現在很多 TCG 平台，其實都面臨類似的問題。

平台必須持續採購卡牌、設計卡池，並承擔庫存壓力。

當用戶成長速度放緩，部分庫存就可能長時間無法流動。

而收藏家手上的卡牌，即使具有市場價值，也未必能迅速找到買家。

https://t.co/NW4jzZ52rr 希望透過共享流動性池，讓兩個原本分開的市場產生連結。

收藏家提供卡牌，開發者提供玩法，玩家提供需求。

卡牌不再只屬於某一家抽卡平台的封閉庫存，而是有機會成為不同應用共同使用的資產。

這也讓我想到 DeFi 的流動性概念。

只是這次共享池裡面的資產，不再只有加密貨幣，而是具有真實收藏價值的 Pokémon、ONE PIECE 或球星卡。

如果這個模式能夠真正運作起來，我認為對整個 TCG RWA 市場會是一個很有意思的發展方向。

🔹 五、TOP MARKET 真正讓我期待的是什麼？
我認為不是單純增加多少種卡池，也不是推出多少高價卡牌。

而是它有機會把三種原本不同的參與者連接起來。

收藏家： 讓自己的收藏品除了持有與出售之外，多一種參與市場的方式。

玩家： 透過不同的應用體驗真實卡牌抽取、保留與回購。

開發者： 不需要自行建立龐大庫存，也有機會推出自己的 TCG 產品。

這三個角色如果能夠形成正向循環，才有機會讓整個共享流動性池持續成長。

不過，我也會持續關注幾個重要問題：
實體卡牌是否真正完成託管與驗證？卡牌估值是否合理？協議的收益來源是否足夠透明？當大量用戶同時要求退出時，流動性又該如何維持？

這些問題都會影響這個模式能不能長期發展。

🔹 最後，我想說的是
我一直認為，TCG 是最有機會與 RWA 深度結合的實體資產類別之一。

因為卡牌本身就擁有收藏文化、價格市場、鑑定制度，以及遍布全球的玩家社群。

過去我們討論的是：
如何把一張實體卡牌帶到鏈上？

但現在我覺得，更值得討論的問題已經變成：

當實體卡牌成功上鏈後，我們究竟能夠為它創造多少新的使用場景？

從收藏、交易、抽卡，到質押、共享流動性與開放式應用。

TOP MARKET 背後的 https://t.co/NW4jzZ52rr 協議，正在嘗試回答這個問題。

目前這套模式仍有許多地方需要透過實際營運來驗證，但至少在產品方向上，我認為它值得 TCG 玩家與 Web3 社群持續關注。

未來的 TCG 平台，競爭的可能不再只是誰的卡池比較好，而是誰能讓每一張真實卡牌，創造更多價值。

這才是我認為 TCG × RWA 最值得期待的未來。

後續我也會深入實測 Top Market 的卡機跟活動，讓大家可以有所比較與了解。

另我覺得比較驚訝的是，Top Market 也有 VAR 驗證機制，這個等之後的文章來跟大家分享。

只是目前 Top Market 才剛上線，還有很多社群跟邀請機制還沒出來，但感覺會跟其他平台打差異化，後續有任何最新資訊旅人會在第一時間跟大家說。

#TOPMARKET #TOPTECH #TCG #RWA

黃金週後第一個交易日：人在路上，錢不在路上
21.44 億人次的流動量與腰斬的票房放在同一張表上，就是彭博說的「假期消費為市場重開蒙上陰影」。更大的變數在月底：五中全會與三季度數據。

簡述
A 股 10 月 8 日結束七天休市重開，午盤滬深 300 跌 0.79% 報 4,323 點，上證綜指跌 0.57% 報 3,820 點，創業板指跌 2.13%，成交額 1.11 兆元人民幣，較節前一個交易日放大近 2,000 億元。半導體、生物製藥、光模組等科技成長股領跌，電池、油氣、港口航運、煤炭、銀行上漲。港股恆生指數自 9 月底以來已跌約 2%。假期同步公布的數據：交通運輸部估計國慶假期跨區域人員流動量 21.44 億人次；商務部監測的 78 個步行街與商圈 10 月 1 至 3 日客流年增 3.4%、營業額年增 5.3%；貓眼數據顯示國慶檔票房到 10 月 5 日才破 8 億元，去年同期八天檔期為 18.35 億元。外匯管理局 10 月 7 日公布 9 月底外匯儲備 3.4 兆美元，單月減少 381 億美元；央行連續第 23 個月增持黃金，持倉達 7,747 萬盎司的紀錄。文旅部的全國出遊人次與總花費截至撰稿時尚未公布。

背景
去年（2025 年）中秋國慶八天長假創下 8.88 億人次出遊、8,090 億元花費的紀錄，但路透據官方數據計算的每人次花費 911 元，是三年來最低，且低於 2024 年的 916 元。今年假期前的訊號就已偏弱：路透 9 月 29 日引述 Forthright Securities 分析師 Ailsa Liao 的「K 型消費」判斷：出遊意願強、人均花費受壓；Dragon Trail 8 月調查顯示 54% 受訪者計畫出境，遠高於去年的 35%，但只有 5% 選擇豪華酒店，33% 選中檔。攜程數據則顯示七晚以上長住訂單年增 123%，旅客走得更遠、住得更久、花得更省。

政策面，人行 9 月下旬以來已降息並注入流動性，節前推出房貸利息補貼與抵押補充貸款（PSL）利率下調。光大證券統計上證綜指 9 月下跌 3.6%。外部環境是假期裡最大的變數：美國十年期公債殖利率假期中一度突破 5.3%，創 2002 年以來新高；英國三十年期公債升至 6%；布蘭特原油站上每桶 100 美元，中東供應中斷與美方可能對伊朗動武的報導推升避險情緒。投資網站引述的日程顯示，中共二十屆五中全會定於 10 月 26 至 29 日召開，與三季度 GDP 公布（通常在 10 月中）接連而至。

分析
彭博 10 月 7 日的標題「疲弱假期消費為市場重開蒙上陰影」點出的核心矛盾，是 2025 年以來一直存在的「財富效應缺席」。去年花旗與野村就在假期後指出，股市大漲對消費的拉動「證據甚少」。今年股市經歷了 9 月的回調，連這個微弱的傳導都不存在了。人流紀錄與票房腰斬並列，說明中國家庭並非不願出門，而是出門時把每一筆非必要支出都壓到最低：長途、長住、低價。這是收入預期問題，不是流動性問題，所以降息與補貼的邊際效果有限。

「消費者仍有強烈的出遊意願，但在花多少錢上保持謹慎。更多旅客不代表成比例更多的利潤。」Ailsa Liao，Forthright Securities 高級分析師，路透 2026 年 9 月 29 日
外匯儲備數字有一個容易誤讀的地方。單月減少 381 億美元，主要是美債殖利率飆升造成的估值損失，而非資本外逃；真正的訊號在黃金：連續 23 個月增持，是在美債殖利率創 24 年新高、美元資產理論上更有吸引力的時候仍在買，表明這是一項不受市場價格影響的戰略配置，目的是降低對美元體系的曝險。對照 9 月華盛頓峰會上「建設性戰略穩定」的氣氛，北京的資產負債表動作比它的外交辭令更誠實。
市場的分歧集中在五中全會。中金稱 A 股可望「強勢開局」，中信建投預期「上有頂、下有底」的區間震盪並建議「AI 算力加創新藥進攻、銀行煤炭公用事業防守」的啞鈴策略；華泰與中泰則把風險放在外部：美國期中選舉後對伊朗施壓、紅海衝突重燃、荷莫茲海峽通行條件。沒有一家券商的核心邏輯是「消費復甦」，這本身就是對假期數據最誠實的解讀。至於外資觀點，賓士第三季在華銷量跌 31% 的數字，比任何宏觀評論都更直接地說明高端消費的狀態。

預測

以下是推測：
50%10 月震盪偏弱。三季度 GDP 與 9 月零售數據確認消費疲軟，五中全會以人事與中長期議題為主，不釋放大規模刺激，上證在 3,700 至 3,900 區間整理。

30%政策驅動反彈。全會前後配合財政加碼（消費補貼擴大、地方化債），A 股重拾 9 月前的升勢，科技股領漲。
20%外部衝擊主導。美債殖利率持續走高或中東升級，北向資金流出，人民幣承壓，央行被迫在穩匯率與寬鬆之間取捨。
盯住的時間點：文旅部國慶出遊人次與花費（看人均是否再創新低）；10 月 13 日前後的 9 月進出口；10 月中旬三季度 GDP 與 9 月社零、固投；10 月 26 至 29 日五中全會公報；月底政治局會議對四季度經濟的定調；11 月深圳 APEC 前的中美貿易休戰（1 月 10 日到期）延長與否。

中國遲到參選世衛總幹事：宋莉是誰，北京要補的是誰的位子

路透 10 月 6 日的獨家說北京「計畫」提名，今天外交部證實。這是美國退出世衛後，中國第一次公開伸手去接那個空位。

簡述
中國外交部發言人毛寧 10 月 8 日在例行記者會宣布，中國提名宋莉競選世界衛生組織總幹事，稱此舉「體現中國對多邊主義和世衛組織的堅定支持」。宋莉現任國家衛生健康委員會婦幼健康司司長，從事婦幼健康政策與國際合作逾二十年。這項提名比世衛 9 月 24 日的報名截止日晚了兩週，但規則允許成員國事後補提。路透 10 月 6 日已引述四名外交官與一名知情人士搶先報導，宋莉與中國駐日內瓦代表團當時均未回應。此前已公開參選的六人分別來自沙烏地、比利時、卡達、波札那、印尼與西班牙。世衛將在 11 月初區域委員會開完後公布完整名單；執行委員會明年 1 月底至 2 月初篩出三人，5 月世界衛生大會投票。譚德塞兩任屆滿，任期至 2027 年 8 月。

背景
美國在特朗普重返白宮後退出世衛，2026 年 1 月正式生效。世衛失去最大金主後進行大裁撤：收縮業務、砍掉高層職位、人力減少約四分之一。中國宣布過追加經費，但路透指出遠不足以填補美國留下的缺口。特朗普政府多年指控世衛在疫情期間「偏袒中國」，稱其為「中國的傀儡」；世衛否認。

宋莉的履歷是典型的技術官僚。山東醫科大學婦產科臨床碩士、北京大學公共衛生博士（2010）、哈佛大學全球健康訪問學者（2010 年下半年）；2002 年進入衛生部婦幼司，2021 年 3 月升任司長。她是世衛母嬰監測顧問組成員，曾任世衛婦幼青少年健康與營養戰略諮詢組成員（2020 至 2023），並共同主持《刺胳針》中國婦幼健康委員會。路透特別提到，2020 年她主編過一份針對中國婦女的新冠防控指引，這會讓她在聽證時面對世衛與中國疫情關係的追問。一個路透沒有寫、但對判斷勝算至關重要的細節是：宋莉 2023 年曾是中國推出的世衛西太平洋區主任候選人，最後敗給東加的皮烏卡拉（Saia Ma'u Piukala）。換言之，她在自己的區域內已經輸過一次。

若當選，她將是繼陳馮富珍（2007 至 2017）之後第二位中國籍總幹事。中國籍官員曾同時執掌四個聯合國機構，如今只剩糧農組織的屈冬玉一人，這也是北京在國際組織人事上的焦慮所在。

分析
路透引述一名外交消息人士的話說得直白：提名的信號是「中國想接手美國空出的角色」。美聯社的 Simina Mistreanu 與 Jamey Keaten 則把它放進更大的脈絡：特朗普退出了數十個國際與聯合國機構，北京在每一個空位旁邊都站著。這是美國缺席帶來的結構性機會，不需要陰謀論解釋。

但機會不等於勝算。對手名單很硬：比利時的 Hans Kluge 是現任世衛歐洲區主任，沙烏地的 Hanan Balkhy 是世衛前助理總幹事，西班牙的 María Neira 長期主管世衛環境與健康部門，印尼的 Budi Gunadi Sadikin 是現任衛生部長，卡達的 Hanan Al-Kuwari 是前衛生部長。宋莉是其中唯一沒有日內瓦管理經驗、也沒有部長級頭銜的人。中國的算盤可能不在「贏」，而在「進三強」：執委會 34 席中，中國憑一帶一路與衛生合作在非洲、亞洲的票源，有能力讓她闖過初選，這本身就是一次政治存在感的展示，也是對未來談判的籌碼。

2023 年西太區主任選舉時，中國連本區的票都沒拿夠。這次挑一個同樣的人選，說明北京看重的是她的技術清白與可控，而非她的票房。飛雨判斷，非引述
中西敘事的落差也值得點出。中方說法是「多邊主義」與「人類健康福祉」；西方媒體的框架是「填補美國真空」與「擴大影響力」。兩者其實不矛盾：對北京而言，多邊主義的價值正在於美國不在場時的話語權。另一個細節是時機：選在美國退出生效、世衛財政最困難、而且就在黃金週結束的第一個工作日宣布，顯示這是一個經過計算、等待美國徹底離場之後才出手的決定，而不是臨時起意。
預測

以下是推測：
45%宋莉進入執委會三人名單。非洲與亞洲票源加上中國的雙邊工作足以讓她過第一關。

20%最終當選。需要歐洲票分裂（Kluge 與 Neira 互相稀釋）且海灣國家兩位候選人互不相讓。
35%初選即出局，北京轉而支持某位全球南方候選人（印尼或波札那）換取其他機構的人事交換。
盯住的時間點：11 月初世衛公布正式候選人名單與各國附帶的經費承諾；11 月的候選人論壇中她怎麼回答新冠溯源與台灣觀察員問題；2027 年 1 月執委會投票；美國是否藉此加碼攻擊世衛「被中國接管」，反而替她在南方國家拉票。

records.text:
Most agent products are built as one person's assistant, then stretched to fit a company. That stretch is where they break.

Recommendation: ★★★★☆
Difficulty: Advanced

QM is a TypeScript agent harness that runs headless on Node with Fastify for HTTP, keeps sessions, memory and queue in Postgres, and reaches users through Slack (a Bolt plugin the core starts and supervises) and a Vite/Lit web app. The unit of isolation is a scope: every person and every room gets its own memory, files, keychain view, permissions, crons and durable sandbox, where installed tools stay installed between turns.

The interesting design choice is that every substrate sits behind an interface. Harness, session store, sandbox and memory are all swappable, and Pi, OpenCode, Codex and Claude Code drive the same core, so a deployment isn't tied to one vendor. Everything company-specific lives in a separate deployment repository that depends on the npm package, so you never check out the source: npm exec --yes --package=@yc-software/qm@latest -- qm init . --org yourorg --target yourtarget, then npm install. To exercise a branch end to end against a real model and real Postgres, npm run dev-instance.

Security is stated rather than implied. An org picks one posture that narrower scopes can only tighten: Strict pauses every harness tool call for approval, Auto screens provenance-labelled external data and tool results through a classifier, Dangerous does neither. A predeclared command policy covering things like recursive deletes and destructive SQL applies even in Dangerous. Set DATABASE_URL and SESSION_STORE=postgres or sessions live in process memory and vanish on restart.

Caveats are real. It's at v0.1.9 and only weeks old, each deployment runs in your own cloud account with no generated CI, and contributions are taken as human-written prose in adrs/ rather than patches. MIT, but this is a system you operate, not a tool you install.

Why Advanced: You supply your own cloud account, Postgres, sandbox image, Slack app and connector credentials before anyone sends a message.

Adoption
14.8k stars, 1.8k forks, MIT license
Used by 16 repositories on GitHub
19 contributors, latest release v0.1.9 (Sep 2026), commits this week

records.text:
冷たい水に毎日手を浸けて、寒さに「慣れる」。それで指は寒さに強くなるのでしょうか？🧊
2012年の実験では、痛みは減ったのに、指先はむしろ少し冷たくなっていました。

今日は「寒さに慣れること」と「指が温まること」は別の話かもしれない、という研究の紹介です。
後半は、ポケットに入る小さな充電式カイロの話をします。

■ 指には「温め直す仕組み」がある
とても冷たい水に指を浸けると、まず指先の血管が細くなります。
体の熱を外に逃がさないためです。

ところが、しばらくすると血管がふっと開いて、指が少し温まります。
そしてまた冷える。これをくり返します。

これを「寒冷血管拡張反応」といいます。
長い名前なので、ここからは「指の温め直し」と呼びます。
1930年に、イギリスの医師トーマス・ルイスが報告した現象です。

昔から「寒い仕事をしている人は、この温め直しが早い」と言われてきました。
たとえば1962年には、イギリスで冷たい魚をさばく仕事の人たちは、ほかの人より温め直しが早く始まった、という報告があります。

ただしこれは、仕事で鍛えられたのか、もともと冷えに強い人がその仕事を続けていたのかを区別できない調査です。
では、実験で冷たい水に慣らしたら、温め直しは強くなるのでしょうか。

■ 学生16人が、15回、冷水に手足を浸けた
確かめたのは、Daanenさんたちの研究チームです(European Journal of Applied Physiology誌、2012年)。

参加したのは、平均20歳の健康な学生16人。男性9人、女性7人です。
右手と右足を、8℃の水に30分浸けます。
冷蔵庫から出したばかりの水に近い冷たさです。
これを週5日、合わせて15回くり返しました。

左手と左足は比べるための側で、最初と最後の2回だけ浸けました。

まず、痛みは下がりました。
0〜10点で答えてもらうと、右手は平均4.5点から2.9点になりました。
つらさには、たしかに慣れたわけです。

ところが、右手の指の温度は上がりませんでした。
浸けている間の平均は、9.28℃から8.91℃へ、むしろ少し下がっていました。
0.4℃ほどの差ですが、偶然のばらつきでは説明しにくい差でした。

「温め直し」が起きる指も減りました。
指1本ずつ数えると、温め直しが1回以上起きた割合は、52%から24%になりました。

つまり、つらさには慣れたのに、指を温め直す働きはむしろ弱まっていたのです。

もうひとつ面白い点があります。
15回浸けていない左手でも、痛みは4.8点から3.9点に下がっていました。
一方で、左手の指の温度は、はっきりとは変わりませんでした。
痛みの感じ方と指の温度は、別々に動いていたことになります。

足は少しちがいました。
右足の指の平均温度は、約0.5℃上がりました。
ただし、温め直しが起きる割合は、はっきりとは変わりませんでした。

条件も書いておきます。
これは健康な若い学生16人が、8℃の水に30分という実験室の条件で受けた結果です。
凍傷そのものを数えた研究ではありません。
15回のあと、変化がどれくらい続くかも調べていません。

■ 著者たちの結論
著者たちは、「凍傷など寒さによるけがを防ぐ方法として、手を冷水に浸ける訓練はすすめない」と書いています。

理由は、指が温まりにくくなったのに、「痛い」という警告のほうが弱まったからです。
ただしこれは、測った温度と痛みから考えた心配です。
けがが実際に増えたことを確かめたわけではありません。

■ 2026年、80本の研究をまとめると
この話は、1本の実験だけではありません。
2026年、Wellerさんたちのチームが、指の温め直しを調べた80本の研究をまとめました(Temperature誌)。
参加者は合わせて2,000人あまりです。

温め直しが始まるまでの時間は、平均すると約8分でした。
ただし研究によるばらつきがとても大きく、3分台から12分台まで幅がありました。
「誰でも8分で温まる」という意味ではありません。

慣らす訓練について、著者たちはこう整理しています。
「一部のやり方では、わずかに慣れた形跡がある。けれど全体としては、実験室で寒さに慣らしても、意味のある改善は出ていない」。
これは数字を計算でまとめた結果ではなく、論文の中で過去の研究を読み比べた部分の結論です。

注意点もあります。
まとめられた研究の参加者は、84%が男性でした。若い人も中心です。
女性や高齢の人に同じことが言えるかは、まだこれからの宿題だそうです。

■ 今日から使えそうな見方
研究から言えるのは、「冷たさに慣れた感覚と、指の温度は、別々に動くことがある」というところまでです。

そこから考えると、「もう慣れたから平気」という感覚は、指が温まっている合図とは限らない、と受け止めておくのがよさそうです。
寒い外で指先が気になったら、慣れで乗り切るより、手袋やポケットで温めておく。そんな素直な選び方で十分かもしれません。

―――
ここからは研究とは別の、道具の話です。
今から紹介する道具は、指の「温め直し」の働きを変えるものではありません。
シンプルに、手を外から温めるための道具です。

■ OCOOPA UT5 Nano(オクーパ)
OCOOPAは、充電式カイロを中心に作っている海外のブランドです。
UT5 Nanoは、持ち歩き向けの小型モデルです。2025年の秋には、海外で新商品として売られていました。
日本では「日本正式上陸」として販売され、2025年の年末からAmazonにレビューが付き始めています。

【先に、気になる点】
・使い捨てカイロに比べると、最初の出費はそれなりにかかります。
・最長約7時間というのは、いちばん低い温度にしたときの目安です。高い温度では短くなります。
・小さいぶん、同じブランドの大きなモデル(UT2Sなど)より、温まる面は小さめです。
・前の晩に充電しておく、というひと手間がいります。
・使い捨てカイロと同じく、低温やけどを避けるため、肌に長く当て続けない使い方が前提です。

【それでも選びたくなる点】
・1個50g以下。Mサイズの卵1個より軽いです。
中に2,000mAhの電池を入れながら、手のひらに収まる大きさにまとめているからです。
ジーンズのポケットや手袋の中、小さめのバッグにも、すっと入ります。

・電源を押して、約2秒で温まり始めます。
使い捨てカイロのように、袋を開けて温まるのを待つ時間がありません。
家を出てから「寒いな」と気づいても、駅のホームで電源を入れれば間に合います。

・2個セットです。
両手のポケットに1個ずつ入れてもいいし、片方を充電しながら、もう片方を使う回し方もできます。

・温度は3段階です。
ぬるめ(約38〜42℃)から、熱め(約48〜52℃)まで選べます。
操作はボタン1つ。長押しで電源、短押しで温度の切り替えです。

・熱くなりすぎると、自動で電源が切れる仕組みが入っています。

・使い捨てではないので、毎日のごみが出ません。

同じブランドの大きなモデルが「電池の量」で勝負しているのに対して、UT5 Nanoは「持ち歩きやすさ」に振ったモデル、という位置づけです。

【誰が使っているのか】
国内ではまだレビューが少なく、どんな人に広く使われているかまでは分かりません。
レビューを読むと、家族への贈り物として選んだ人が目立ちます。
「最初は自分用に買ったけれど、子ども用にした。あったかいと喜んで学校に持っていっている」という声もありました。
Amazonでは、海外分や色違いも合わせて3,000件を超える評価が付いています。

【買ったあとの、冬の朝】
冬の朝、駅のホームで電車を待つ5分間。
今はコートのポケットの中で、冷えた指を握ったり開いたりしているかもしれません。

これがあると、家を出るときに電源を押して、ポケットに入れておくだけです。
手を入れた瞬間、そこにもう温かいものがある。
片手でスマホを見ている間も、もう片方の手は温かいまま。
寒い朝が少しだけ楽しみになる、そんな小さな変化です。

【向いている人・向かない人】
向いているのは、通勤や通学で外を歩く時間がある人。
使い捨てカイロのごみを減らしたい人。
小さなバッグで出かけることが多い人です。

向かないのは、一日中外にいて、長い時間ずっと使いたい人です。その場合は、電池の大きいモデルのほうが合います。
充電を忘れがちな人も、使い捨てカイロのほうが気楽かもしれません。

電源を押して2秒、卵より軽いものがポケットの中で温かくなる。温まるのを待たなくていい、というのがいちばんの違いです。

参考文献
・Daanen HAM, Koedam J, Cheung SS. European Journal of Applied Physiology, 2012(オンライン公開は2011年) (DOI: 10.1007/s00421-011-2233-4)
・Weller RS, Buczny J, Daanen HAM. Temperature, 2026 (DOI: 10.1080/23328940.2026.2646391)
・Nelms JD, Soper DJ. Journal of Applied Physiology, 1962
・Lewis T. Heart, 1930

―――

If you dunk your hands in cold water every day until you "get used to it," do your fingers actually get better at handling the cold? 🧊
In a 2012 experiment, the pain went down, but the fingers ended up slightly colder, not warmer.

Today's topic: getting used to the cold and keeping your fingers warm may be two different things. After that, a small rechargeable hand warmer that fits in a pocket.

■ Your fingers have a built-in "rewarming" trick
Put a finger in very cold water and the blood vessels in the fingertip narrow first. That keeps body heat from leaking out.

But after a while, the vessels suddenly open up and the finger warms a little. Then it cools again, and the cycle repeats.

Scientists call this cold-induced vasodilation. It's a mouthful, so let's just call it "finger rewarming." The British physician Thomas Lewis described it in 1930.

People have long said that those who work in the cold rewarm faster. A 1962 report, for example, found that British fish filleters, who handle cold fish all day, started rewarming earlier than other people.

But a survey like that can't tell whether the job trained their hands, or whether people with cold-tolerant hands were simply the ones who stayed in the job. So what happens if you train people in cold water on purpose?

■ 16 students, 15 cold-water sessions
That's what Daanen and colleagues tested (European Journal of Applied Physiology, 2012).

The volunteers were 16 healthy students, average age 20: nine men and seven women. They put their right hand and right foot into 8°C (46°F) water for 30 minutes, about as cold as water straight from the fridge. They did this five days a week, 15 sessions in total.

The left hand and left foot were the comparison side. They only went into the water at the first and last session.

First, the pain dropped. On a 0-10 scale, the right hand went from an average of 4.5 to 2.9. People really did get used to the discomfort.

But the right-hand fingers did not get warmer. Their average temperature during immersion went from 9.28°C to 8.91°C, slightly lower. It's only about 0.4°C, but it was too large to put down to ordinary variation.

Rewarming also became less common. Counting finger by finger, the share of fingers that rewarmed at least once fell from 52% to 24%.

In other words, the discomfort faded while the fingers' rewarming response actually weakened.

There's another interesting detail. Even the untrained left hand hurt less by the end, going from 4.8 to 3.9. Yet the left-hand finger temperatures didn't clearly change. Pain and finger temperature were moving separately.

The feet behaved a bit differently. The right toes got about 0.5°C warmer on average, but the share of toes that rewarmed didn't clearly change.

The conditions matter here. These were 16 healthy young students, in a lab, with 8°C water for 30 minutes at a time. The study didn't count actual frostbite, and it didn't follow people after the 15th session to see how long the changes lasted.

■ What the authors concluded
The authors wrote that they do not recommend repeated cold-water hand immersion as a way to prevent cold injuries such as frostbite.

Their reasoning: the fingers got harder to warm while the "this hurts" warning signal got weaker. That concern is an inference from the temperatures and pain scores they measured. They did not show that injuries actually increased.

■ 2026: pooling 80 studies
This isn't just one experiment. In 2026, Weller and colleagues pulled together 80 studies of finger rewarming (published in the journal Temperature), with a little over 2,000 participants in total.

On average, rewarming started about 8 minutes into immersion. But the studies varied enormously, from around 3 minutes to around 12. It doesn't mean everyone's fingers rewarm at 8 minutes.

On training, the authors summarized it this way: some protocols show limited signs of adaptation, but overall, getting people used to the cold in the lab has not produced meaningful improvement. That conclusion comes from the part of the paper that reads through earlier studies, not from the pooled calculations.

There's a caveat. 84% of the participants in the pooled studies were men, and most were young. Whether the same holds for women and older people is still an open question for researchers.

■ A way to think about it starting today
What the research supports is this much: the feeling of being used to the cold and the actual temperature of your fingers can move separately.

So it's probably wise not to treat "I'm used to it now" as a sign that your fingers are warm. If your fingertips feel cold outside, simply warming them with gloves or a pocket may be a better bet than toughing it out.

―――
Now for something separate from the research: a piece of gear. This product doesn't change your fingers' rewarming response. It's simply a way to warm your hands from the outside.

■ OCOOPA UT5 Nano
OCOOPA is an overseas brand focused mainly on rechargeable hand warmers. The UT5 Nano is its compact, carry-anywhere model; it was already on sale overseas as a new product in autumn 2025. In Japan it's sold as an official Japan launch, and Amazon reviews started appearing at the end of 2025.

Downsides first:
- It costs more up front than disposable heat packs.
- The "up to about 7 hours" figure is for the lowest heat setting. Higher settings run shorter.
- Because it's small, the warm surface is smaller than the brand's bigger models such as the UT2S.
- You need to remember to charge it the night before.
- As with disposable heat packs, avoid keeping it pressed against the same patch of skin for a long time, to prevent low-temperature burns.

Why it's still worth a look:
- Each unit weighs 50 g or less, lighter than a medium egg. It packs a 2,000 mAh battery into something that fits in your palm, so it slides into a jeans pocket, a glove, or a small bag.
- It starts warming about 2 seconds after you press the button. No tearing open a pack and waiting for it to heat up. Even if you only notice the cold after leaving home, you can switch it on while waiting on the platform.
- It comes as a pair. Put one in each pocket, or use one while the other charges.
- Three heat levels, from mild (about 38-42°C) to hot (about 48-52°C). One button: long-press for power, short-press to switch levels.
- It shuts itself off automatically if it gets too hot.
- It's reusable, so there's no daily trash.

Where the brand's bigger models compete on battery size, the UT5 Nano is built around being easy to carry.

Who's using it: In Japan, reviews are still few, so it's too early to say who uses it most. Reading through them, a lot of people bought it as a gift for family. One reviewer said they first bought it for themselves, then gave it to their child, who happily takes it to school because it's warm. On Amazon, counting overseas reviews and other colors, it has more than 3,000 ratings.

What changes on a winter morning: Picture the five minutes you spend waiting for the train on a cold platform. Right now you might be clenching and opening your cold fingers inside your coat pocket. With this, you press the button as you leave home and drop it in your pocket. The moment your hand goes in, something warm is already there. While one hand scrolls your phone, the other stays warm. A small thing, but it can make a cold morning feel a little more welcoming.

Good fit: people who walk outside on their commute or school run, people who want less heat-pack trash, and people who go out with a small bag.
Not a good fit: people who are outdoors all day and want hours of continuous heat; a bigger-battery model suits them better. If you often forget to charge things, disposable packs may be less hassle.

Press a button, and two seconds later something lighter than an egg is warming up in your pocket. Not having to wait is the biggest difference.

An AI code review can help a team inspect a change. It should not become the release control that decides whether the change is safe to merge. That distinction matters when a program plan counts review comments as risk reduction without checking whether reviewers found real defects or missed important ones.

GitHub’s Copilot agent application card says code review may miss problems, raise false positives, and produce suggestions that are incorrect or insecure. GitHub advises users to review and test suggestions and to supplement Copilot review with careful human review. These are the vendor’s stated product limitations, not an independent estimate of error rates. (GitHub Docs, “Application card: GitHub Copilot Agents,” accessed 2026-10-07, https://t.co/j3z4h4po6x)

DORA’s 2025 report summary describes AI as an amplifier of an organization’s existing strengths and weaknesses. The summary says returns depend on the underlying organizational system, not only the tool. The public landing page supports that broad statement; it does not provide the detailed numerical results needed for a metric claim. (DORA, “State of AI-assisted Software Development 2025,” https://t.co/OJZ1AO9Qtk)

A TPM can turn those cautions into a release test. Track how many AI findings engineers accept, reject, or cannot reproduce. Keep existing tests, security analysis, and code-owner review in the merge path. Sample merged changes to check for escaped defects and measure review delay separately from defect detection. If the AI creates more comments but the team spends longer sorting false alarms, the workflow may be adding load rather than reducing risk. Those measures are proposed for local evaluation; neither GitHub nor DORA claims they are universal KPIs.

Set a limited pilot with an owner, a comparison period, and a rollback condition. Keep the AI reviewer advisory until the team has evidence from its own repositories. Revisit the gate when language mix, change size, or review policy shifts. That is a more defensible release decision than treating a vendor feature description as proof of quality.

#TPM #CodeReview #SoftwareDelivery

【ニッスイ 不正アクセス「商品が出せない」】
｜
ニッスイのグループ会社、日水物流が使っている一部サーバーへの不正アクセスが発覚
→商品の入出庫が停止

ニッスイによると、グループが管理する個人情報などの外部流出の有無は現在調査中

▼スーパーでは在庫状況を懸念
スーパーセルシオ和田町店 食品バイヤー
久保田浩二さん
「メーカーから『商品が出せない』と連絡が来てしまうと、あすあさって売るものが、急ぎ手配すべき状況になり得る」

「そこが一番心配が残っている状況」

(Q.今ある在庫は何日分)
「店にあるもので、きょうとあす2日分しかない」

「大きな影響が出ますという発表がメーカーからされてしまうと、店としても対応が早急に迫られてしまう」

客(40代)
「遠い話かなと思っていたが、食品会社に及んでくるとなるとちょっと心配にはなる」
「日々使っているものだから、なくなったら困る」

▼原因はクラウドサービスのシステム障害
ニッスイはクラウドサービスを利用
↓
膨大なデータをインターネット上で管理する“データの保管場所”のようなもの

サービスは、ソフトバンクの子会社IDCフロンティアが提供
↓
利用する企業や団体は保育サービスなど、行政のホームページなど495に及ぶ

IDCフロンティアによると、7日午前3時40分ごろ、福島・白河市にあるサーバーの一部がデータを暗号化して身代金を要求する“ランサムウェア”による攻撃を受ける

茨城県によると、担当者から「サーバーの電源が落ちた」との連絡
↓
県や県警のホームページが閲覧不可に

IDCフロンティア
「かなり深刻な状況だと捉えています」
「まだ調査の段階で、当社のクラウドサービスの復旧見通しは立っていません」

▼日本政府も対策へ…
日本政府は関係省庁会議を開き、不正アクセスなどの情報は、NCO(国家サイバー統括室)に集約することを決定

また、企業などへデータの適切な管理や、不必要な情報の削除を求めることなどが話し合われた

古川俊治デジタル大臣
「大変危急の状況となっている。政府一丸となって対策を進める必要がある」

デンマークでは2日、デンマーク版「マイナンバーカード」が登録されたデータベースが悪用された
↓
880万人分の名前、個人識別番号などが登録
↓
デンマーク政府が注意を呼びかけ

▼サイバー攻撃急増の背景にAI
イスラエル発のサイバーセキュリティ会社の調査によると、簡単な指示をするだけで、役割を与えられた一般に公開されているAIが、ほぼ自律的に遂行していたことが判明

サイバー攻撃などからウェブサイトを守る都内の専門企業に、攻撃の実演を特別に協力してもらった

サイバーセキュリティクラウド
セキュリティーエンジニア牧瀬拓巳さん
「AIを使ったツールで攻撃していく」

「いまサイトの偵察をAIでしている」
「例えば“空き巣”に入るイメージ。窓が開いてないか見ていって、開いた場所があったら入りこむ」

「何を盗むかタスクとして上がっていて、実行している。それを全部AIがやっている」

AIの情報を元に処理を行うと、住所や電話番号などの個人情報の一覧が表示

サイバーセキュリティクラウド
セキュリティーエンジニア牧瀬拓巳さん(29)
「AIだからできるというより、AIだから早い」

「人間が一つ一つハッキングするよりかなり短時間で、知識がない人でもできちゃうところが、母数を増やしている可能性」

▼個人情報が闇サイトで取引される場合も
SNSなどのアカウント160億件が、3万9000ドル(約617万円)で売りに出されていた

サイバーセキュリティクラウド
代表取締役CTO 渡辺洋司さん
「160億件は日本の人口よりも多いですし、世界中のアカウントがここで売られてしまっている可能性も」

「これまではハッカーといわれるような人たちが、高度なスキルを持っていないと見つからないケースが多かった」

「生成AIをいっぱい並べて実行することによって、その脆弱性を見つけることが非常に安易になっている」

「攻撃が増える、攻撃がしやすくなった背景になっているんじゃないか」

MORNING WATCH — OCTOBER 8

Three things to watch this morning:

🇪🇹🇪🇷 The Ethiopia–Eritrea situation is getting much more dangerous.

There are now several reports that Eritrean troops have crossed into northern Tigray.

Two residents in Adigrat said they saw two trucks carrying dozens of Eritrean soldiers through the town on October 7. A commander from the government-aligned Tigray Peace Force separately told that Eritrean troops entered Adigrat on October 6 and Idaga Hamus a day later.

ACLED says Eritrean troops crossed at Zelambesa on October 7 and were later hit by drones attributed to the Ethiopian military around Guada.
If this report holds up, this is a very different situation from the one we were watching a few days ago.

Until now, the argument was largely about Eritrean support for the TPLF and whether Asmara might intervene more directly. We may now be looking at Eritrean soldiers physically inside Ethiopia and potentially already coming under Ethiopian attack.
That is exactly how the Tigray war starts becoming an interstate crisis rather than just another phase of Ethiopia’s internal conflict.

I’d still be careful with the scale. Two trucks and several reported crossings do not tell us whether this is a limited deployment, reconnaissance, reinforcement of local allies or the beginning of something much larger.

And we still don’t know whether Eritrean forces are coordinating directly with the TPLF.

—

🇮🇷 Hormuz is starting to hurt shipping again.

At least 12 attacks against tankers and LNG/LPG carriers were recorded in the week ending October 5, according to maritime-security data cited by Reuters  the highest weekly total since the war began.

There was another incident in the last 24 hours.
The Antigua and Barbuda-flagged chemical tanker Acers was hit by several projectiles around 51 nautical miles off Qatar. UKMTO reported the incident, while maritime-security sources said some crew members suffered minor injuries.

More important than the headline number, though, is what shipowners are doing.
Traffic through Hormuz has now fallen to its lowest level in more than two months.

The next thing to watch is whether Iran actually begins enforcing the restrictions it announced near the Omani side of the strait. Seizures, repeated interdictions or another sharp fall in traffic would tell us this is moving from harassment into something more systematic.

—

🇹🇼🇨🇳 One more thing that is new to us, even though it happened in August.

Reuters has published an investigation into what appears to be the first known sighting of a Chinese maritime-militia vessel off Taiwan’s east coast.

A private surveillance aircraft operated by Taiwan’s Apex Aviation spotted the fishing vessel Minfudingyu 07902 more than 30 nautical miles off Hualien in mid-August.

It was in the same area as Chinese Coast Guard vessel 2502 and the research ship Xiang Yang Hong 03. Two Taiwanese officials confirmed the vessel identifications to Reuters.

So seeing a militia-linked fishing vessel there alongside Chinese state vessels is worth noting.
But I wouldn’t jump from one sighting to “China is rehearsing the blockade.”

We don’t know whether the three ships were operating together, how long they stayed there or whether this has happened repeatedly without being detected.

If militia vessels start appearing east of Taiwan regularly, alongside Coast Guard or research ships, then we may be looking at a real expansion of China’s maritime presence around the island.

—

🇾🇪 Yemen / Saudi Arabia

The Houthis have claimed another ballistic-missile attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. AP reports explosions, evacuations and a temporary closure, while Saudi authorities say several missiles were intercepted.

Generated docs usually rot the day after they're generated. The interesting part here isn't the writing, it's the run state file that survives an interrupted job.

Recommendation: ★★★★☆
Difficulty: Intermediate

It's a TypeScript CLI (Node 22 or newer) that points a documentation agent at your repository and writes a linked Markdown wiki into openwiki/, which you own and commit. It also does a personal mode for your own notes, and ships an interactive graph visualizer you can export as a static site.

① Install with npm install -g openwiki, then run openwiki --init at the repo root. The first run walks you through picking one of thirteen providers, a key and a model. Rerunning --init regenerates the whole wiki but preserves your hand-written openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md brief. On a persistent checkout, an interrupted run resumes from openwiki/.run.json and its durable page queue; ephemeral CI runners start over.

② openwiki --update covers changes since the last successful run plus stale Claims. Claims are the part worth reading about: material facts carry versioned source evidence, so when that evidence moves or disappears the tool knows which statements need confirming, rewriting or retiring instead of silently keeping a lie in the docs.

③ For automation, copy examples/openwiki-update.yml into .github/workflows and let it open a docs-only PR. The README is unusually careful here: use a fine-grained token with Contents and Pull requests read/write as OPENWIKI_PR_TOKEN, because PRs opened with the default GITHUB_TOKEN won't trigger pull_request checks. Keep add-paths restricted to generated docs and don't auto-merge workflow files. Alternatively run it inside your coding agent with openwiki integrations install claude (or codex, opencode, cursor) and reuse that agent's model.

Caveats: it's MIT but young, v0.5.1 with a long open issue list, and every run costs provider tokens on a repo-sized corpus. On Windows, install via npm or pnpm; bun can fall back to compiling better-sqlite3.

Why Intermediate: Needs Node 22, a model provider key with real token spend, and CI plus token setup to get the self-updating part working.

Adoption
16.4k stars, 1.2k forks, MIT license
Used by 16 repositories on GitHub, 18.9k downloads on npm in the last week
80 contributors, latest release v0.5.1 (Sep 2026), commits this week

🧭SpaceXはGrok Botの裏で他社のClaudeも使う | 法人向けのCursorでは、他社モデルを使うたび100万トークン0.25ドルを上乗せしている $SPCX

Grok を作っている会社が、自社の看板のエージェントに、他社のモデルを使うと言い出した。

SpaceX $SPCX の Elon Musk は10月7日、自社の AI エージェントについてこう書いた。

> Grok Bot について大事なお知らせだ。今後 SpaceX は、どの作業にも最良のバックエンドのモデルを使う。Claude Opus 5.5、Midjourney、Suno など主要な API も含めてだ。いちばん良い結果につながりそうなものを使う
> （Elon Musk, SpaceX CEO）

Grok Bot は8月に始まったサービスで、クラウド上のコンピューターを使って動く。利用者のアプリにログインし、仕事を最後まで進める。月20ドルの Cursor のプランなどに含まれている。Grok を含む SpaceX の AI セグメントは、4〜6月期に売上の33%を占めた。Grok Bot の開始と Cursor の買収は、この四半期のあとになる。

名前を挙げた中に、自社の Grok は入っていない。SpaceX には、モデルを作る以外の稼ぎ方もある。利用者と各社のモデルの間に立ち、作業をそれぞれに合うモデルへ割り振る側（オーケストレーション）に回ることだ。その形を、すでに子会社の Cursor で作っている。

コードを書くための AI ツール Cursor は、8月14日に SpaceX の傘下に入った。法人向けのプランで「Auto」を選ぶと、依頼ごとにどのモデルへ回すかを Cursor が決める。料金は、回した先のモデルの定価で数える。

この法人向けのプランでは、他社のモデルを使った分に上乗せがある。利用者が自分で選んでも、Auto が回しても同じだ。AI が読み書きする量はトークンという単位で数え、上乗せは100万トークンごとに0.25ドルかかる。利用者が Anthropic などと自分で契約したキーを持ち込んでも、この上乗せは残る。自社の Grok と Composer は対象外で、月額に含まれる利用量も多めに取ってある。

割り振りで変わるのは、利用者が払う作業1件の料金だ。AI が書き出す100万トークンの定価は、同じ料金表で Claude Opus 5.5 が20ドル、Grok 4.7 が6ドル。3倍強の開きがある。重い推論だけを Claude に回し、残りを安いモデルで済ませるほど、1件の料金は下がる。

SpaceX は自社のサポート窓口を Grok Bot に任せ、費用の下げ方を公開している。よくある問い合わせを分類し、ヘルプページの確認で済むものには重い調査をさせない。解決1件の費用は、安いもので0.2〜0.3ドルまで下がったという。従来の AI サポートのツールは解決1件1〜4ドルの定額だ、と SpaceX は比べている。

割り振る側にも、自分では決められないものがある。並べられるのは、売ってくれるモデルだけだ。

8月29日の記事では、Cursor に並ぶモデルを決めるのは、買った SpaceX ではなく売る側だと書いた。OpenAI は買収のあと、Cursor へのモデル提供を11月12日で止める案を SpaceX に通知している。今回 Musk が Grok Bot の裏に置くと名指しした言語モデルは、Anthropic の Claude だった。

SpaceX が Grok Bot で取りに行くのは、モデルの順位より、利用者と各社のモデルの間に立つ位置だとみている。Cursor の法人向けでは、その位置にいるだけで、Claude が働いた分からも取り分が出ている。

その位置の値打ちは、自社の Grok の出来より、Anthropic のような売り手が並び続けるかで決まっていくだろう。

AI News Digest — October 8, 2026

The last 24 hours were dominated by two frontier product launches, an unverified math dump from an unreleased model, and a cluster of capital and policy moves around compute and evaluation.

Model releases

OpenAI began rolling GPT-6 into ChatGPT on October 7, with GPT-6 Sol on paid tiers and GPT-6 Luna reaching Free and Go on October 8. The release is paired with Intelligent UI, which can return tappable controls, calculators, and editable charts instead of plain text. OpenAI says this covers more than 1.2 billion weekly users. It matters because the default consumer interface is shifting from text answers to model-composed interactive tools at global scale.

Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7 (claude-haiku-5-5) at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens, which it says is about 90 percent below Haiku 4.5 on that band and roughly 75 percent lower on average. It is the first Haiku with an effort control, a 1 million-token context, and published computer-use scores (72.4 percent on OSWorld 2.1 in Anthropic’s own tests). It matters because high-volume agent and routing workloads just got an order-of-magnitude cheaper at the small-model tier.

NVIDIA said a fine-tuned Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (550 billion total parameters, 55 billion active) scored 535.4/600 at IOI 2026, above the gold cutoff of 361.12 and the top human score of 498.27, and 30/42 at IMO 2026 against a gold line of 29. This is a company claim from a single source. It matters if the contest conditions hold, because it would put a specialized open model above the best human contestant on live olympiad tasks.

Perplexity released pplx-embed-v2-late, open-weight late-interaction embedders at 0.6 billion and 9 billion parameters, covering text, images, and rendered pages. Liquid AI also opened weights for d1-3B, a single-forward-pass decision model aimed at edge hardware. These matter for retrieval and on-device classification, not for frontier reasoning.

Research

OpenAI published 722 mathematical manuscripts, grouped into about 372 families, produced by an unreleased internal model after roughly 4,000 problems and about three hours of ChatGPT Pro compute per result on average. Results are under Apache-2.0; Lean formalizations are incomplete, and OpenAI says some unformalized claims may be wrong. It matters because a closed model is now generating a public corpus of claimed solutions to open problems faster than the community can check them.

Epoch AI’s InnovationEval, dated October 7, tested whether models can invent a post-training method that beats a strong GRPO baseline on Qwen3-8B. The best run reached about 40 percent of the gain from a published human method; Epoch’s verdict was no. It matters because it is a direct, negative result on automated AI R&D under a fixed compute budget.

Funding and infrastructure

Nous Research confirmed a $90 million Series B at about a $1.5 billion valuation (one report cites $1.2 billion), taking total funding to roughly $158 million, and is packaging Hermes for enterprise use. It matters because an open-agent stack with large download volume now has a priced enterprise path.

Chan Zuckerberg Biohub’s Virtual Biology Initiative reached $1.8 billion in commitments on October 7. Google DeepMind, Meta, and Isomorphic Labs added $300 million; the Department of Energy is putting in more than $500 million over five years. It matters because the bottleneck for biological foundation models is labeled cell data, not another general chatbot.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Broadcom is arranging more than $50 billion in financing for the custom chips it is building with OpenAI. That is project finance, not an equity round. It matters because OpenAI’s inference supply is being tied to a dedicated silicon program at that scale.

Butterfly Effect, parent of the Manus agent, closed a round of more than $500 million at a $4 billion valuation after the Meta deal unwound. DeepSeek’s larger China raise, reported near $12–15 billion and a roughly $74–75 billion valuation ahead of a Shanghai listing, is still in term-sheet reporting rather than a closed round.

Policy

Senator Maria Cantwell released a six-point framework under which NIST would set safety rules for frontier models, with ongoing audits and mandatory incident reporting. It is a proposal, not enacted law. It matters because it is the clearest current Senate outline for federal pre-release testing.

The Pentagon’s Tradewinds marketplace is awarding some AI contracts in under a week from five-minute vendor pitches, with agents that could support weapons targeting listed as a priority. Finland ordered Google to stop work at two planned data centers after forest clearing began before the environmental review was finished, holding part of a roughly €13 billion build. The first changes procurement speed; the second shows power and land permits can stop a hyperscale site after capital is committed.

答案是风冷。HPE 发布 ProLiant Gen13 首批四款，旗舰 DL585a 给风冷机房用。

配置：
· 2 颗第六代 AMD EPYC，每颗最多 256 核、600 瓦
· 8 张双宽卡，或 16 张单宽液冷卡；首发可订英伟达 RTX PRO 6000 系列
· 32 个内存插槽，最多 8TB；16 个 E3.S 盘位，PCIe 6.0
· 15 组 80 毫米双转子风扇，可热插拔
· 电源：系统 2 个，加 GPU 8 或 12 个，每个 3200 瓦，N+N 冗余
· 满配 117 公斤，2027 年春上市，没有公布价格

为什么做这么高：HPE 在发布会上说，企业客户现有的机房大多还是风冷，而且往往是机柜的电先用完，空间还剩着。所以宁可做高，留出风道。

同批另外三款：DL525 是 1U 单路，11 月最先上市；XD245、XD285 是多节点机型，2027 年上市。

七小服做服务器和 GPU 过保维保，7×24×4 响应。能修的修，该换的换。

records.text:
Buying 128GB of DDR5 RAM to offload large models onto a single RTX 3090 will not fix the physical speed penalty of system memory.

A single 24GB 3090 running Qwen 27B can comfortably hit ~60 tokens per second with 150k context. The moment you look at running larger quants with Strata offloading, the immediate impulse is dropping serious money on a Ryzen 9700X and 128GB of 6000MHz RAM.

Except DDR5 bus bandwidth is nowhere close to GDDR6X. Overspilling active model weights into system RAM inevitably craters generation speed. The people reporting 90 to 120 tokens per second on large UD quants are keeping those weights almost entirely inside multiple 3090s, not offloading across a consumer motherboard.

Even if you want to test offloaded weights, jumping straight to 128GB is pure overkill. A setup with 64GB of system memory already fits quants like UD-Q4_K_XL alongside the 24GB card.

If fast coding throughput matters for your daily work, keeping your model entirely inside VRAM is still the line that counts. Don't rebuild your entire PC on offload hype until you verify whether the output actually justifies the speed drop.

records.text:
Anthropicから、新モデル「Claude-Haiku-5.5」が先ほど公開されました。以下ではサイバーセキュリティに関わる記述を中心に、コスト面と主な特徴もあわせてまとめています。まず価格は前のHaiku-4.5の10分の1でOpenAIのGPT-6-Lunaと同額ですが、GPT-6-Lunaを6指標すべてで上回ります。また、MaxとTeamプランの契約者には今週から、Claude-APIで任意のモデルに使える月額クレジット（Max-5xは100ドル、Max-20xは200ドル、Teamは席数に応じて組織全体で最大500ドル）を付与。

サイバー能力はHaiku-4.5から大きく向上したものの、Opus-5.5やMythos-5.1だけでなく、前世代のOpus-5にも及ばないとの評価。多段階の攻撃シナリオを実行させる評価「CyScenarioBench」の達成率は3.3%で、Sonnet-5.5の46.1%、Opus-5.5の67.6%と開きがあります。この能力に応じて、サイバーの安全対策はHaiku-4.5より厳しい一方で最近の他のモデルより対象を絞り、特定の有害行為だけをブロック。

Sonnet-5.5より広い範囲の防御作業を許可し、ペネトレーションテストなど攻撃者が用いることの多い技術は引き続きブロックされます。ブロック時に別モデルで応答する仕組み（フォールバック）はなく、より広い作業が必要な組織には、10月6日に3段階へ拡大されたCyber-Verification-Programへの申請が案内されています。

間接プロンプトインジェクションの評価（Gray-SwanのIPIベンチマーク、攻撃者が15回試行した条件）では、攻撃成功率がHaiku-4.5の83.2%から7.1%に低下。残る弱点はGUIでのコンピュータ操作（24.4%）で、Sonnet-5.5の3.4%やOpus-5.5の1.0%には届かず、GPT-6-Astraの8.5%と同程度とされます。

コスト面では、Haiku-5.5の運用費は平均でHaiku-4.5より約75%低下。あわせてSonnet-5.5のキャッシュ読み取りを0.20ドルから0.10ドルに半減（エージェント作業で約20%減）、MaxとTeamプランの契約者には今週から、Claude-APIで任意のモデルに使える月額クレジット（Max-5xは100ドル、Max-20xは200ドル、Teamは席数に応じて組織全体で最大500ドル）を付与。Claude-Codeの対話利用やプランの上限超過分には使えず、未使用分の繰り越しもありません。
Haikuとして初めて推論強度の設定を備え、SDKにはコンピュータ操作とブラウザ操作の対応がベータ版として加わります。

【要点の整理】

・サイバー能力の評価は安全対策オフで実施。ExploitBench（V8の脆弱性41件）で任意コード実行に至った割合は1.0%、Binary Exploitation Benchmarkの制御フローハイジャックは3件（Opus 5.5は106件、Sonnet 5.5は50件、Haiku 4.5は0件）

・Claude Codeでの悪意ある依頼の拒否率は84.3%（Haiku 4.5は66.6%）、デュアルユース・正当な依頼に対応した割合は98.9%。コンピュータ操作での有害な依頼の拒否率82.59%はSonnet 5.5・Opus 5.5（各79.46%）を上回る

・プロンプトインジェクション耐性はコーディング0.2%、ツール利用4.0%と高く、コーディングとコンピュータ操作の環境での適応的攻撃に対する評価ではSonnet 5.5・Opus 5.5・Fable 5.1と同等

・サイバーの安全対策は特定の有害行為をブロックする分類器のみで、自社製品とAPIではフォールバックなし。生物分野の安全対策はSonnet 5・Sonnet 5.5・Opus 5と同一

・拡大後のCVPはDefense Access（防御作業、数日で審査）、Red Team Access（許可を得たペネトレーションテスト、数週間で審査、組織のみ）、Specialized Access（人命や市場に影響しうるシステムの試験、米政府と共同で審査）の3段階。Opus 5.5・Sonnet 5.5・Mythos 5.1と今後の新モデルが対象

・価格は10万トークンを超える分が入力0.50ドル・出力2.50ドル。Haiku 4.5は1ドル・5ドルで、10万トークン以下の依頼は旧Haikuの約90%

・比較表ではGPT-6 Lunaを6指標すべてで上回り（OSWorld 2.1は72.4%対48.9%、Terminal-Bench 4.0は39.2%対16.4%）、Sonnet 5.5には全指標で及ばない。複雑なエージェント型コーディングにはSonnet 5.5・Opus 5.5の方が向くとの説明

・RSPの閾値を新たに越えることはなく、自動化された行動監査では試験したどのモデルより過剰拒否が多い。気づかれにくい妨害行為の能力は大型モデルよりはるかに低いとの評価

Haiku 5.5は、サイバー能力が限られる小型モデルに対して安全対策の対象も絞る、能力に応じた方針を採ったとの説明です。プロンプトインジェクション耐性は上位モデルに近づきましたが、GUIでのコンピュータ操作では開きが残る状況。数値はAnthropicのシステムカードによるもので、サイバー能力とプロンプトインジェクション耐性はいずれも製品に組み込む防御を外した条件での測定です。

https://t.co/9ES7tuarBl
